hypothesis: Pooling normalization moments over unrelated TRAIN scenes may alter the fixed focal scene representation/confidence when only its batch mate changes. This is a task-relevance diagnosis, not an assumption that BatchNorm is harmful.
first_test: Actual source-derived BatchNorm configuration/learned affine, float32/64 exact focal feature rows with matched-count independent mates; pooled vs separate-scene training moments. Repeat/within-scene row permutation/eval-stat negatives. Actual trained W2 confidence head must remain batch-separable for fixed inputs.
required_native: Fixed native focal TRAIN item with two prespecified mates, dropout disabled in every arm, BN train vs fixed-stat-only control, same frozen weights/RNG/GT and restored buffers. Preserve upstream sampling and point correspondences; confidence/IoU direction and repeat error must be reported, not inferred from CPU.
sampling: Scene cluster is independent unit; component rows are not task samples.
limits: No validation tuning, new model package, queue admission, GPU use or normalization replacement until native mechanism evidence. Do not reopen an existing rejected route.
